claim: In the matching retail DLL, Menu_SoundManager.Play_RefereeVoice (0x060052A9) is a static two-parameter method named vid:Int32 and volume:Boolean? No: its exact signature blob is 00020111aa380c, with vid:Int32 and volume:Float32, and an exact 122-byte body. It returns when static Sound_ClipRefereeVoice_List is null, returns when vid is negative or vid is 24 or greater, and returns when Sound_ClipRefereeVoice_List[vid] is null. It computes local volume = Volume_Voice * volume. The emitted bge.un against raw 0.0f means ordered-negative values return, while greater/equal or unordered values continue. It then compares the local against raw 1.0f using ble.un; ordered values greater than 1.0f are replaced with raw 1.0f, while values less/equal or unordered continue unchanged. It selects raw audioSrcInfo index 4, loads its sRefAudio field, calls UnityEngine.AudioSource.set_volume(local), then calls UnityEngine.AudioSource.PlayOneShot(Sound_ClipRefereeVoice_List[vid]) on the same sRefAudio and returns. FACT-0076 pins the direct caller with arguments vid and fixed raw 1.0f.
